record.context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of non-curve Aubry-Mather sets
record.original_question: For a C^r twist area-preserving diffeomorphism with r≥3, is the union of the action-minimizing invariant sets that are neither closed curves nor periodic orbits always of Hausdorff dimension 0?

evidence.quote: they are also called action minimising sets. Problem 3.1.4 (M. Herman) For a Cr twist area-preserving diffeomor­ phism does the union of the action-minimising sets which are not closed curves and do not contain periodic orbits have Hausdorff dimension O?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A = \mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{T} \times [0,1]$) be the annulus, and let $f : A \to A$ be a $C^r$ area-preserving diffeomorphism with $r \ge 3$ satisfying the twist condition (in suitable coordinates $(x,y)$, lifting $f$ to $\tilde f(x,y) = (X(x,y), Y(x,y))$ on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$, one has $\partial X/\partial y > 0$). An $f$-invariant set $K \subset A$ is called action-minimizing (Aubry–Mather) if it is the support of an invariant Borel probability measure that minimizes the average of a generating-function action among all $f$-invariant probability measures with the same rotation number; equivalently, every orbit in $K$ is globally action-minimizing with respect to a generating function for $f$. Define
$$ \mathcal{M}(f) = \bigcup \bigl\{ K : K \text{ is an action-minimizing invariant set of } f,\ K \text{ is not a closed (rotational) invariant curve, and } K \text{ contains no periodic orbit}\bigr\}. $$
Is it true that $\dim_H \mathcal{M}(f) = 0$, where $\dim_H$ denotes Hausdorff dimension?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (attributed to M. Herman) about whether the union of non-curve, periodic-orbit-free Aubry–Mather sets of a smooth twist area-preserving diffeomorphism has Hausdorff dimension zero is reported as an open problem in dynamical systems. While related results exist (e.g. work on hyperbolic Aubry–Mather sets being C¹-irregular and on Hausdorff dimension of the Mather quotient by Fathi–Figalli–Rifford), no proof or counterexample resolving Herman's question appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The link between the shape of the Aubry-Mather sets and their Lyapunov exponents
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses irregularity and geometry of Aubry-Mather sets for twist maps without resolving Herman's dimension question.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on Aubry-Mather set regularity exist but the dimension question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: AIM dynamics open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems in dynamics related to Aubry-Mather theory and Hausdorff dimension of invariant sets.
status_evidence.claim: Herman-type questions about Hausdorff dimension of Aubry-Mather sets are listed as open.
